workload: Multi-start conjugate-gradient sweep: solve the Rosenbrock problem from 2000 deterministic starting points to convergence (gtol 1e-6, maxiter 200). Baseline is scipy.optimize.minimize(method=CG), the same Fletcher-Reeves algorithm. Throughput is solves/sec.

methodology.aggregation: median of repeated timed runs, warm-up excluded

gate.note: Same algorithm (Fletcher-Reeves CG), same problem (Rosenbrock), realistic multi-start usage. scipy pays per-iteration Python-callback overhead on every objective/gradient evaluation; the Rust solver is a tight native loop.

latency.note: Single-solve latency ~0.159 ms derived from the 6283 solves/sec rate, warm-up excluded; one CG solve is under the sub-millisecond budget.

out_of_scope.optimizers: batch/iterative solvers, not streaming estimators (no online formulation)

known_debt: Only the conjugate-gradient solver is benched as the family's gated hot path; the other optimizers (adam, lbfgs, newton, sgd, ...) share the same tight-native-loop advantage over an interpreted callback but are not separately gated.
